Watchlist methodology

Daily RS = Stock daily close ÷ SPY daily close · Weekly RS = Stock weekly close ÷ SPY weekly close

A stock qualifies for the daily list when its RS is strictly greater than the highest RS value across the preceding 63 (3M), 126 (6M) or 250 (12M) trading sessions. The current session is excluded from each comparison. A ticker appears if it had at least one breakout in the latest 10 completed sessions. This identifies relative-strength leaders to monitor; it is not an entry signal.

The weekly RS-leads-price signal is triggered when weekly RS (stock weekly close ÷ SPY weekly close) equals or exceeds its highest value across the preceding 52 completed weeks, while the current week’s stock high remains below its highest weekly high across those same preceding 52 weeks. Once triggered, the signal remains active for up to 20 completed weeks even if RS no longer makes a fresh high. It exits if a subsequent weekly high reaches or exceeds the then-relevant prior 52-week price high. A newer qualifying RS event resets the signal age. “Signal date / age” shows the trigger week and weeks elapsed; “Price vs 52w high” shows the latest weekly close relative to the current prior 52-week high. Only completed weekly candles are evaluated.

Eligibility filters: share price above $10; 30-day average dollar volume above $30 million; 10-day average share volume above 350,000 shares; 14-period ADR% above 4%; biotech stocks included. Dollar volume is calculated as 30-day SMA multiplied by 30-day average share volume.

Data and coverage

TradingView's public screener supplies the NASDAQ, NYSE and AMEX common-stock and depositary-receipt universe. Daily OHLC data for stocks and daily closes for SPY come from Yahoo Finance via yfinance. Every stock series is aligned to SPY's exact trading dates before calculating relative strength. These are public data interfaces, not an institutional market-data service. Newly listed shares with insufficient history cannot qualify. Use the list to find candidates, then assess pullbacks to support or moving averages, price action, volume and risk/reward on the chart before considering an entry.
